summary.headline: RateGain Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR785 crores (up 188% YoY, 17.5% organic) and FY27 margin guidance was raised to 22.5-23.5%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was RateGain's highest-ever quarter, with revenue of INR785 crores and adjusted EBITDA of INR193.4 crores at a 24.6% margin, helped by a one-time USD2.5 million FIFA World Cup uplift. Organic growth for the combined Sojern-Adara entity was 17.5% YoY in INR terms. Management raised FY27 revenue guidance to around INR3,100 crores (upper end of the earlier range) and adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 22.5-23.5%, up about 100 bps. Debt repayment continued, with USD47.5 million repaid (38% of the acquisition loan), and management expects to be net debt-free by FY28.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR6.8 crores in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: Net debt INR615.4 crores; cash INR255.6 crores; net worth INR2,114.2 crores (as of June 30, 2026)

segments.name: Martech
segments.commentary: Now over 81% of revenue; grew 341% YoY on consolidation of Sojern, with organic growth of about 18.2%. Destination, property and corporate sub-segments all cited growth, with APMEA new customer wins up 200% YoY.

segments.name: DaaS
segments.commentary: Grew 22.7% YoY with healthy performance across Air, OTA and Car. Management expects airline large deals and revAI order book to add upside.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: Grew 3.1% YoY, described as modest. Management is betting on Agentic ARI, RateIQ and the direct stack, and expects double-digit growth by fiscal year end.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue now expected at the upper end of the prior range, around INR3,100 crores, implying 70% YoY growth and double-digit growth for the combined base.
FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance raised to 22.5-23.5% from 21.5-22.5%.
One-time FIFA uplift of USD2.5 million is not expected to repeat at the same scale in Q2; management expects revenue to normalize marginally.
Management aspires to grow 15-20% in the near to medium term and sees the higher end of that range for FY27 exit; it expects Q3 and Q4 to be stronger.
Sojern deferred consideration of about INR80-90 crores a year (INR20-22 crores per quarter add-back) runs until Q3 FY29.
FCF conversion of 75% or better expected for full FY27; net debt-free by FY28.
Gross margin expected to remain around 70% in the near term; management says upside is possible but will not commit yet.
M&A expected in 2027, not in 2026, despite debt prepayment.
capex_capacity: Debt: additional USD16 million repaid after quarter end; cumulative USD47.5 million repaid (38% of original loan), outstanding USD77.5 million.
Shared AI-powered platform across Martech, Distribution and DaaS; no capacity or capex figures disclosed.
Product launches in Q1: Parity Plus next generation, ChatGPT ads on property, AI Digest for AirGain, Uno Viva extended to 50+ languages including WhatsApp.
Property-side team unification complete in APAC; Europe and US still to be unified, which management expects to accelerate deal velocity.
demand_pricing: Middle East revenue fell from about USD970,000 a month pre-disruption to about USD425,000 a month currently; treated as a headwind with recovery potential.

Pricing power: management says discounting need has fallen since Sojern and Adara stopped competing; a regional Indian chain is being signed at higher outcome-based fees; destination competitors are weak and one approached RateGain to be bought out.
Contract wins are reported as new logos only and exclude upsizing of existing customers; management is revising KPI reporting. The quarterly run rate of about INR96-98 crores was cited by an analyst.
RateIQ is in discussions with about a dozen customers; management cited 10-100% booking uplifts for some chain pairings. Uno Viva is near a very large Middle East customer win.
Airbnb is a customer, not a competitor; management says it provides connectivity and DaaS to Airbnb.

qa_highlights.question: Are there examples of pricing power in the combined entity, and will deal velocity improve after people integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited reduced need to discount in destinations, higher outcome-based fees with a large Indian regional chain, and weaker distant competitors. It expects deal velocity to rise as the Europe and US property teams are unified.

qa_highlights.question: Is organic growth in INR and could the exit run rate near 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed 17.5% organic growth is in INR. Management sees the higher end of the 15-20% range and expects acceleration in Q3 and Q4, while noting FIFA is not large and revenue is mostly recurring.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin impact of the one-off items?
qa_highlights.answer: Net one-off of about USD1 million (USD2.5 million FIFA less about USD1.5 million Middle East dip), with about 70% gross margin implying roughly USD600,000-700,000 of EBITDA benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Can Sojern alone be assumed to run at about 30% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to attribute margins; synergies come from both Adara and Sojern and the businesses are now one team and platform, so attribution is not possible.

qa_highlights.question: Why are contract wins and distribution growth low?
qa_highlights.answer: Contract wins count only new logos and understate upsizing. Distribution grew 3.1%; management expects double-digit growth by year end on direct stack and RateIQ traction, plus airline large deals in DaaS.

qa_highlights.question: Is Martech organic growth disclosed separately?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Martech grew about 18.2% organically; it declined to split Sojern from Adara because teams and platforms are unified.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin outlook and M&A?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin is expected to stay similar near term; a rise is possible but not committed. M&A is possible in 2027 but nothing expected in 2026.

risks_watch: One-time FIFA uplift (USD2.5 million) and Middle East revenue decline (about USD1 million a month lower) affect Q1 comparability; Q2 normalization.
Distribution growth (3.1%) lags DaaS and Martech; newer launches need to convert to revenue.
Contract-win KPI definition is being revised, so the reported figures are not comparable with prior disclosures.
Deferred Sojern consideration of INR80-90 crores a year runs to Q3 FY29, while other income fell sharply to INR3.1 crores.
Management did not attribute margins between Adara and Sojern, which limits visibility into the acquired business's economics.
summary.management_tone: Confident and optimistic on growth and margins, with management raising guidance. It was less forthcoming on specifics: it declined to split Sojern and Adara figures, would not commit to a gross margin increase, and was vague on contract-win metrics.
key_quotes: We now expect full-year revenue to come in at the upper end of the range we shared with you last quarter, around INR3,100 crores for FY27.

On margins, we now expect adjusted EBITDA margins of between 22.5 % to 23.5% for FY27, roughly 100 basis points or 1 percentage point uplift from the earlier 21.5 % to 22.5% range I shared with you last quarter.
This quarter marked a shift from building the foundations on one RateGain to operating as one company.
Airbnb is a B2C. It's in the area of vacation rental. Airbnb is actually a big customer of RateGain.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided to upper end of range, around INR3,100 cr (~70% YoY, largely acquisition-driven), with adjusted EBITDA margin raised to 22.5-23.5%; backing is partial (product launches, RateIQ pipeline, Airline deals, FIFA one-off) with no capacity or order numbers, and organic aspiration is 15-20%.

rows.label: Airline large deals and revAI order book in DaaS

rows.label: Net debt-free by FY28
